title: Latency-prioritized pin & throttle orchestration for multi-region routing
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Purpose: implement an orchestration policy that prioritizes low-latency region affinity (pinning) while respecting region capacity constraints via throttles and soft-eviction, and that integrates circuit-breaker triggers and graceful load-shedding. This ticket covers design, simulation, config surface, rollout plan, and initial implementation for the request director service.

Motivation: customers require consistent tail latency SLOs across global user bases. Naive geo-pin behavior can cause overload in popular regions. We need a policy that: (1) preserves locality when it meets SLO windows, (2) automatically shifts traffic when regional capacity degrades, and (3) degrades gracefully with clear telemetry and fast rollback.

Goals:
- Keep p95 user-visible latency within SLOs for 95% of customers while minimizing cross-region hop cost.
- Avoid sudden regional saturation by bounding pinned traffic using capacity-aware throttles.
- Provide deterministic circuit-breaker rules to eject regions from pinning when internal signals indicate overload.
- Implement soft-eviction (spillover) that prefers compatible fallback model variants instead of hard drops.

Non-goals: full autoscaler rewrite; network-level routing changes; per-token pricing changes.

Design summary: the policy composes three signals into a region score: latency_headroom_score, capacity_headroom_score, and error_stability_score. A weighted aggregation yields a runtime-steer-score per region for each customer shard. Routing decision algorithm (high-level):
1) If customer is pinned to region R and R.steer_score >= pin_threshold, route to R.
2) Else evaluate top-K regions by steer_score and pick region with highest score subject to capacity budget slots for this customer class.
3) If no region meets steer_score >= fallback_threshold, trigger global fallback: either route to dedicated fallback pool or return a controlled 429 (configurable per-customer).

Key signals and thresholds:
- latency_headroom_score: based on (SLO_latency - observed_p95) normalized to [0,1].
- capacity_headroom_score: derived from GPU_utilization, request_queue_ms, and token_backlog estimate. Uses exponential smoothing to avoid flapping.
- error_stability_score: 1 - recent_error_rate (windowed 1m & 5m).
- pin_threshold: default 0.6 (tunable by customer tier).
- fallback_threshold: default 0.35.

Circuit-breaker policy: two-level breakers: region-level and customer-affinity-level. Region-level CB trips when: sustained p50/p95 growth over baseline, GPU OOMs, or sustained autoscaler-impaired state. CB actions: mark region as in_avoid for routing decisions and start cooldown timer with exponential backoff.

Load-shedding approach: prefer model-variant fallback (quantized / lower-context) when available. If not, apply token-level shedding with a prioritizer that keeps short completions over long streaming jobs. Provide transparent error metadata to the app (x-redwood-shed-reason).

API/config surface: add new director config block (example below). Config is runtime-changeable via Console and flaggable per customer.

Example config (YAML snippet):
routing_policy: latency_pin_throttle_v1
pin_threshold: 0.6
fallback_threshold: 0.35
weights:
  latency: 0.5
  capacity: 0.35
  error: 0.15
capacity_budget:
  per_customer_slots: 50
  global_spill_percent: 10
circuit_breaker:
  region_failure_rate_window: 60s
  trip_error_rate: 0.05
  cooldown_seconds: 120
load_shedding:
  prefer_model_variant: true
  token_shed_priority: ["short-completions", "interactive", "long-batch"]

Telemetry and SLOs: we will create a dedicated dashboard with these metrics:
- p50/p95/p99 by customer-region affinity
- steer_score per region and distribution by customer
- pin_hit_rate (percent of requests served by pinned-region)
- region_capacity_score and global_spill_percentage
- shed_rate and shed_reason breakdowns
- SLO burn rate and error budget per customer class

Rollout plan:
- Phase A (sim): run offline simulation for 2 weeks using production traces (traffic replay) and synthetic capacity alarms. Evaluate predicted pin_hit_rate and expected shed_rate.
- Phase B (canary): enable policy for 1% of global traffic (internal customers first) for 3 days, monitoring burn rate & error signals.
- Phase C (gradual ramp): 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with safety gates at each step (no >2x error budget burn rate, p95 within 10% of baseline).
- Phase D (customer opt-in): expose config in Console for customers to enable early.

Chaos and testing: run regional failover drills with simulated node OOMs and slow GPUs. Inject artificial queue growth to validate soft-eviction paths. Add unit and integration tests for scoring math and CB transitions.

Security and compliance: no customer data movement changes. Policy respects VPC routing and tenancy. Audit logs required for any automatic pin overrides.

Operational playbook (short):
- If p95 spikes and steer_score for primary region drops: check capacity_score and autoscaler events. If region-level CB tripped, follow 'region evacuation' runbook (see attachments).
- If shed_rate rises above threshold: reduce pin_threshold by 0.1 for affected customers and force a canary rollback.
- For observed incorrect ejections: validate smoothing window and increase hysteresis.

Stability trade-offs and decisions:
- We favor conservative capacity_score hysteresis (smoothing) to avoid flip-flopping on momentary load bursts.
- Default weights tilt toward latency to preserve SLOs; capacity dominates when utilization exceeds 70%.
- Cost trade-off: some cross-region traffic increase tolerated to keep SLOs; we will surface estimated cross-region egress to customers.

Next work items:
- implement scoring microservice and expose steer_score as gRPC endpoint (ENG-50321.1)
- add director config binding and Console controls (ENG-50321.2)
- create simulation harness and run with 30 days of replay trace (ENG-50321.3)
acceptance_criteria: Scoring service returns steer_score for any customer-region pair with <10ms median latency
Director uses steer_score to change routing decisions in canary mode without impacting >2x error budget burn
Dashboards created and alerting rules for pin_hit_rate, shed_rate, and steer_score anomalies
Circuit-breaker transitions visible in audit logs and reversal action documented
Simulation results demonstrating <1% additional SLO misses compared to baseline under synthetic 20% region load spike
playbook: On region-level CB trip: mark region in_avoid, route pinned customers to next-highest steer_score, notify SRE oncall
If shed_rate > 0.5% for >5m: reduce pin_threshold for affected customer cohorts by 0.1 and open incident
If p95 increases >25% for pinned cohort: trigger rollback to previous routing policy flag
If autoscaler reports insufficient nodes for >3m: trigger emergency spillover to fallback pool and escalate
